assessment: This study presents strong and compelling evidence that the extra-cellular matrix protein SVEP-1 interacts with the TIE1 receptor to promote aspects of lymphangiogenesis that are independent of canonical VEGF-C signaling. Using zebrafish models to show genetic interactions and cells to provide evidence of biochemical interaction, the study shows a functional requirement for these genes/proteins in specific aspects of lymphangiogenesis. These novel findings will be of interest to developmental and cell biologists and to those studying lymphatic disease as it potentially provides novel therapeutic targets.
